capabilities.verb: Keep your health records on your own server
capabilities.summary: Self-host on Linux with Docker: the database, uploaded files and task queue stay on your infrastructure, with no managed cloud tier.
proofs: Nothing phones home — data lives where you deploy it
LLM API keys are Fernet-encrypted at rest and masked in responses
Prompt-injection screening on AI input; audit log on every clinical write
Export to a FHIR Bundle or ZIP backup with a SHA256 manifest
Rotate your password, revoke any device, and every session ends immediately

capabilities.verb: Ask your own records questions in plain language
capabilities.summary: The chat assistant answers from your biomarkers, medications and documents with citations back to the source, and proposes every write for your approval.
proofs: Answers cite the records they draw from
Proposes, never writes: every change opens a review card you approve
Works with any OpenAI-compatible provider, including local vLLM or Ollama

capabilities.verb: Compare lab results across labs and over time
capabilities.summary: The biomarker engine normalizes results from different providers to a common unit and charts each marker longitudinally against its reference range.
proofs: Results from different labs auto-convert to a common unit
Every result is scored 0.0–1.0 inside its reference range
Trend charts flag normal versus abnormal values over time

capabilities.verb: Add a missing drug, allergen or biomarker to your catalog from one dialog
capabilities.summary: From any record form, open the catalog browser and define the missing item once — it becomes a reusable, tenant-wide reference instead of one-off free text.
proofs: The catalog browser's New action opens the typed definition form per catalog (medication, allergy, vaccine, biomarker)
AI assist drafts medication definitions (description, indications, dosage, contraindications, side effects) on request
Created items are visible across the whole health record and every create is audited (catalog_audit_log)
Identity is server-owned: the record links to the new definition by id, never by typed name

capabilities.verb: Share your record with the people who treat you
capabilities.summary: Grant your doctor or a family caregiver access to specific records with a chosen permission level and optional expiry - you decide who sees what, and you can revoke in one click.
proofs: Patient-initiated sharing is request-based: the invited staff member must accept before any record is visible
Grants are ranked read/write/admin, optionally expiring, and revocation takes effect immediately
Every grant, acceptance, decline and revocation is audited and notifies the affected party
Clinic staff can be scoped to assigned patients only (tenant setting) instead of the whole tenant

capabilities.verb: Bring curated catalog content in from your own sources
capabilities.summary: Register git repos, registries or file uploads as seed-pack sources: every pack is digest-pinned, admin-approved and applied with full provenance, precedence and tenant overlays.
proofs: Every pack version is digest-pinned and applied only after an admin approves that exact digest
Revoking a version re-applies the previous one and restores what it retired — rows are retired, never deleted
Remote fetches run through the SSRF-guarded transport with pinned refs and size/time caps; credentials live only in a secret slot
A user-edited row always wins; adopting an available pack update is an explicit, audited action
The Sources surface reviews the per-stage plan and keeps audited run history; the export emits the canonical pack, re-ingested zero-write

capabilities.verb: Turn lab reports into structured, searchable data
capabilities.summary: Snap a photo or drop a PDF of a report, letter or discharge summary; an OCR + AI pipeline extracts biomarkers, medications and findings for your review.
proofs: Handles lab reports, doctor letters, imaging and discharge summaries
Magic Fill maps pasted clinical text onto structured examination fields
Extraction runs in the background worker, off the API process

capabilities.verb: Follow a pregnancy, condition or recovery across visits
capabilities.summary: Clinical events group the examinations, results and notes of one journey into a single timeline with custom fields like trimester or pain intensity.
proofs: Seeded journey types — pregnancy, pain episode, surgical recovery — carry their own field schemas
Every journey links back to the examinations and results that fed it
Journeys are stored as FHIR Condition resources, exposed on the R4 facade
Type blueprints, categories and templates localize with the app

capabilities.verb: Bring in data from wearables, apps and clinics
capabilities.summary: Bundled connectors pull wearable and hospital data — Withings over OAuth2, hospital FHIR servers over SMART-on-FHIR — and an HMAC-verified webhook receives pushes from custom senders.
proofs: Pulls records from hospital FHIR servers over SMART-on-FHIR with PKCE
The bundled Withings connector pulls weight, blood pressure, heart rate and SpO2 over OAuth2
The inbound webhook verifies HMAC-SHA256 signatures with replay protection
Official bridge client SDKs ship for Python, TypeScript and Kotlin
An MCP client connection exposes external tool servers to the assistant

capabilities.verb: Put appointments on a calendar you own
capabilities.summary: Publish examinations and clinical events to Google, Microsoft 365, Nextcloud, iCloud, Fastmail, CalDAV or an ICS feed. Detail is redacted by default.
proofs: Default redaction shows only “Medical appointment” — never the reason
Full detail is opt-in and requires explicit confirmation
Credentials live in the sealed store; binding rows hold only a pointer
Inbound events are attributable-only — lookalikes need your confirmation
Providers, scopes and destinations come from a shared catalog

capabilities.verb: Get medication reminders and out-of-range alerts
capabilities.summary: Scheduled reminders and event-driven threshold alerts fan out to the in-app inbox and Web Push, with per-kind preferences and digest collapsing.
proofs: Medication and follow-up reminders fire on Celery beat schedules
Threshold alerts evaluate on observation ingestion — a bad result alerts immediately
Delivery is real-time in-app (WebSocket) and Web Push (VAPID)
Per-kind preferences with inline mute and digest collapsing

capabilities.verb: Extend it with your own integration providers
capabilities.summary: The Integration SDK authors bundled extensions: one validated manifest declares capabilities and data classes, and the engine never probes provider internals.
proofs: One validated manifest gates every declared capability at registration
BaseHealthProvider, BaseConfigFlow and ObservationBuilder ship in the SDK
OAuth2 + PKCE, rate-limit handling and cursor-based delta sync included
A ten-chapter doc set starts with a ten-minute quickstart

capabilities.verb: Set your organization's security rules per tenant
capabilities.summary: Require MFA per role, cap session idle time and lifetime, limit concurrent sign-ins, and restrict logins to an IP allowlist — all enforced immediately, all audited.
proofs: Require TOTP MFA per role; SYSTEM_ADMIN can never opt out
Idle and lifetime session windows are enforced on every request and refresh
Concurrent-session limits evict the oldest device automatically (audited)
CIDR IP allowlists gate login and refresh; denials answer ip_not_allowed
Every policy change is audited with a before/after diff of the changed keys

capabilities.verb: Watch and export a tamper-evident audit trail
capabilities.summary: Admins browse their tenant's audit stream with full filters and export it as CSV or JSON — every row carries its position in the SHA-256 hash chain, so deletions or edits are detectable.
proofs: Filter by actor, resource, action, outcome and date range, newest first
Exports stream CSV or JSONL with chain metadata (chain_key, seq, prev_hash, entry_hash)
Tenant admins see their own tenant; SYSTEM_ADMIN sees the system-wide view
The export itself is recorded in the audit stream
A chain verifier walks every entry and alarms on any gap or mismatch

capabilities.verb: Open an audited emergency-access window
capabilities.summary: Break-glass is a time-boxed, two-person-approved elevation: staff request a widening of permissions they already hold, a second admin approves, every use is audited and the window auto-expires.
proofs: Two-person law: the requester can never approve their own window (enforced by a database CHECK)
Tenant windows need a second ADMIN; system windows a second SYSTEM_ADMIN
Only permissions the requester already holds can be widened, capped at 240 minutes
Every transition and every use under a window writes a tamper-evident audit row
Windows auto-expire; single-admin hosts recover through the documented host rescue runbook

capabilities.verb: Integrate clinics over a standards-based FHIR R4 API
capabilities.summary: An OAuth2 + SMART-scoped FHIR R4 facade serves 20 resource types with CapabilityStatement, search Bundles, Provenance-on-write and soft-delete tombstones.
proofs: 20 R4 resources — Patient, Observation, Condition, MedicationStatement, DiagnosticReport and more
SMART-on-FHIR scopes and OAuth2 gate every external request
Every write records Provenance; deletes leave 410 Gone tombstones
Search returns FHIR Bundles with pagination and OperationOutcome errors

capabilities.verb: Sign in with your work identity
capabilities.summary: Each tenant can bind its own OpenID Connect provider (SSO) and push users and groups through SCIM 2.0 — with link-only identity binding, no account merging, and full audit trails.
proofs: Sign-in verifies the provider-signed ID token (PKCE, state, nonce, JWKS) — the identity provider never signs your internal session tokens
Link-only identity: one external identity maps to exactly one account in one tenant; verified email required, never merged
An SSO address matching an existing account confirms the link while signed in — it is never silently attached
JIT provisioning is capped by allowed domains and a group-to-role map that can never grant admin-only roles
SCIM deprovisioning kills every live session immediately; directory tokens are hashed at rest, shown once, revocable instantly

capabilities.verb: See every device, sign out the rest, prove presence for dangerous actions
capabilities.summary: Every sign-in is listed with its device, address and last activity; sign out one device or all the others without losing yours. Role changes, exports, break-glass and admin grants ask for a fresh password or TOTP first.
proofs: Every sign-in is listed with device, IP and last seen; revoke one or all others without losing your own session
Role changes, exports, break-glass and admin grants require a fresh password or TOTP proof within ten minutes
A sign-in from an unseen device raises an in-app/push alert
SSO sign-ins obey the same MFA and IP policy as password logins

capabilities.verb: Sign in with a passkey, not a password
capabilities.summary: Register Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key as a passkey. It satisfies the tenant MFA policy, signs you in with user verification and steps up sensitive actions; the private key stays on the device.
proofs: The authenticator's private key never leaves your device; the server stores only the public key and a signature counter
A passkey assertion requires user verification (biometric or device PIN), not just possession
A passkey satisfies the tenant MFA policy exactly like TOTP; password sign-ins then offer either factor
A cloned authenticator (signature counter regression) is disabled and audited immediately
Role changes, exports, break-glass and admin grants can be proved with a passkey

capabilities.verb: Automate your records with a scoped token
capabilities.summary: Mint personal access tokens for scripts, CLIs and home automation. Each token carries only the permissions you pick, can be limited to specific patients or none, expires and rotates, and never becomes a full session.
proofs: The token value is shown once; only a hash and a lookup prefix are stored
Every request is authorized by the token's own permission subset, re-checked against your current role
Patient scope limits a token to all reachable records, an explicit list, or none, and revoked care-team grants narrow it immediately
Expired, revoked and cross-tenant tokens stop working at once; rotation replaces a token and revokes its predecessor in one step
A token can never create another token, start a session or change your password, MFA or passkeys

capabilities.verb: Connect devices and labs without handing over your account
capabilities.summary: Every integration and extension runs as its own scoped identity instead of acting as the person who connected it. It gets only the permissions and patients you approve, and revocation is immediate.
proofs: A connector acts as a service identity with its own permission subset, never as your role
Scopes are re-checked on every use against your current role and the extension's declared capabilities
Patient scope limits a connector to your reachable records, an explicit list, or none
Revoking the principal stops it immediately, even mid-sync; rotation replaces the secret and retires the old one
Undefined extension capabilities are refused by the host, and extension code never receives direct database access

useCases: Compare cholesterol across two labs after switching providers — drop both PDFs, get one unit-normalized trend line scored against its reference range.
Track a pregnancy visit by visit — start the seeded journey, fill trimester fields, link each examination, read the whole timeline in one place.
Catch an out-of-range result the day it lands — threshold rules evaluate at ingest and push a Web Push alert to your phone.
Pull your hospital record onto your own server — connect the clinic's FHIR server over SMART-on-FHIR and let cursor-based sync bring new results in.
Manage your household's records under one install — one record per person, role-scoped views, per-person dashboards and journeys.
